output.summary: The yield fall is real: gauge R&R is stable and the CMM program, calibration and criteria are unchanged. New operators do not reject more than experienced ones, so the August cohort is not the cause. Reject rates roughly doubled on all six lathes while the Corvane within-lot hardness spread widened, and the long-shaft lathes L3-02 and L3-05 have runout above the 5 um limit and the highest reject rates. Their tighter journal tolerance confounds that comparison. Fatigue and the shift change are untested because no hour-of-shift data was collected. Several causes may overlap. Reverting shifts and blaming Corvane are premature, and punishing operators or sampling inspection would be harmful. Run the staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trial lots and hour-of-machining matching.
